title: Tail-latency-aware health sampler and autoscale smoothing for regional SLO preservation
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: During cross-region failovers and bursty traffic we observe probe flapping driven by transient tail-latency spikes (p99) which causes the autoscaler to oscillate and triggers aggressive regional failover. That behavior degrades end-user SLOs and increases cost due to unnecessary scale churn.

Goal: Implement a tail-latency-aware health sampling layer combined with autoscaler-signal smoothing and a short-term circuit breaker so that readiness/liveness decisions and autoscaler inputs reflect sustained degradation rather than instantaneous spikes. The solution should be runtime-agnostic (apply to hosted/Dedicated/Private) and integrate with existing probe instrumentation and the autoscaler public interface.

Proposed approach:
1) Health sampler: probabilistic sampler that weights probe samples by recent tail-latency contribution (p95/p99 windows) and request contract. The sampler emits health samples at a stable rate, biasing detection toward sustained tail events without overreacting to single-request noise.
2) Signal smoothing: autoscaler consumes an EWMA and a median-filtered window of the health score instead of raw probe counts. Smoothing parameters are configurable per-region and per-service class (latency-sensitive vs. best-effort).
3) Short-term circuit breaker: when a region sees rapid degradation, mark region as degraded for a short cooldown and route traffic to fallback capacity instead of immediately triggering global failover. Circuit breaker has state machine with counters exposed to Console.
4) Evaluation harness: extend the existing synthetic-warmup simulator to replay customer-shaped tail spikes, run 1000 simulated failovers, and measure autoscaler thrash, p95/p99, and cost delta.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We bias toward tail events to protect p99 SLOs, which may delay detection of fast catastrophic failures; to mitigate, we keep a small fast-path detector that triggers immediate emergency-flush when observed error-rate > 5% over 3s.
- Smoothing increases detection latency; we tuned EWMA windows to preserve SLOs under common workloads (see acceptance criteria).
- Implementation touches probe collection and autoscaler ingestion points; we will keep a backward-compatible feature flag and rollout with canary routing.

Why this is different from previous work: Current work has focused on probe gating, fanout reduction, and hierarchical damping. This ticket targets the specific failure mode of tail-latency-driven probe noise causing autoscaler thrash during region failover and combines probabilistic sampling with autoscaler-side smoothing and a tactical circuit breaker.

Deliverables: design doc, simulator results, instrumentation changes, autoscaler smoothing primitives, console metrics and circuit-breaker dashboard, canary rollout and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=50% reduction in autoscaler scale-up/scale-down cycles during failover replay compared to baseline
No regression in p95; p99 improves or holds within 5% of baseline under nominal traffic
Canary in eu-west-1 passes for 48h with feature flag on and no manual intervention
Circuit breaker triggers correctly in simulated rapid degradation and routes traffic to fallback capacity per policy
Metrics emitted for health-sampler weight, EWMA signal, and circuit-breaker state are visible in Console and documented
